lines.trans: Well, hello! Are we playing musical chairs with guest luggage before the concert?
Mazen checked in two rooms without his glasses right before the early-train call, Suad!
Did you say EARLY train?! What time is our honoured mapmaker arriving today?!
Three sharp this afternoon, madam—three hours ahead of the printed card.
Good heavens! Rami and I have not finished rehearsing the middle bridge of our duet!
Do not worry, Suad; here sits the striped hatbox safe and sound outside Room Six!
And both green backpacks are parked neatly on the bench beside Room Two.
Let me write two polite calligraphy cards so the guests swap brass tags at the desk.
Oh, thank you, Suad—your handwriting makes even a key mix-up look five-star!
Tuck one card on hook two, one card on hook six, problem solved before one.
Now tell me where Rami is hiding—we need thirty solid minutes at that walnut piano!
He just walked through the courtyard gate—meet him inside Room Nine right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

انحل.gloss: to dissolve; come untied; be solved

meanings.en: to dissolve (in water); to be solved or untied
meanings.note: Form VII medio-passive of حل ('to untie / solve'). Used for ink running in water or a knot coming undone.

examples.trans: Blue ink dissolves quickly in water.
The problem was solved calmly.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بالضبط.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بالضبط.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (long aa in the past, ii in the subjunctive/present). Often used in the sense 'to look/seem'.

examples.text: الألوان بتبان أحلى تحت ضوء الشمس.
examples.trans: The colours look prettier in the sunlight.
After two minutes the true story became clear.

meanings.note: Levantine 'want' built from بد- plus pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بدنا (we want).

examples.trans: What do you want to do now?
I wanted to talk with you.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Form II verb from بدل. Used for alternating colours or swapping items.

examples.trans: We alternated between gold and white.
I need to swap out the wet bag.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Italian prova; used across Arabic for music rehearsals, theatre runs, and tailoring fittings.

examples.text: عندنا بروفة الساعة خمسة في القاعة.
examples.trans: We have a rehearsal at five in the hall.

examples.text: بعد تلت بروفات صارت الفرقة جاهزة.
examples.trans: After three rehearsals the band was ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخبى, بيتخبى).

examples.trans: Why did you hide behind a mysterious note?

examples.text: القطة تخبت تحت الطاولة من المطر.
examples.trans: The cat hid under the table from the rain.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Feminine noun from علّق ('to hang'): a wall peg, hook, or hanging tag.

examples.text: المفتاح معلق على أول تعليقة جنب الباب.
examples.trans: The key is hanging on the first hook beside the door.
Put the apron on the hook once you finish.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Relative adjective from اثنين ('two'): describes a musical duet or a pair working together.

examples.trans: They played a duet section on piano and violin.
A two-person performance needs good coordination.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حفلات.

examples.trans: He designs concert halls.
We attended a lovely music concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Colloquial feminine noun from خربط ('to mess up/mix up'). Used for small administrative or scheduling mix-ups.

examples.text: صار في خربطة بسيطة بالمواعيد بس انحلت.
examples.trans: There was a small mix-up in the times, but it got sorted.

examples.text: مكتبي صار خربطة من كتر الأوراق.
examples.trans: My desk became a mess from so many papers.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطوط.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Used in the mild exclamation يا ساتر! ('goodness! / heaven forbid!').

examples.trans: Goodness, I nearly dropped the glass!
Goodness, what heavy rain outside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Numeral 'six'; short form ست (sitt) before a plural noun (ست سنين 'six years').

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسجل, بيسجل).

examples.text: سجلنا بالغلط حجزين على غرفة سبعة!
examples.trans: By mistake we booked two reservations into room seven!
I wrote the name down in the big ledger.

meanings.note: Paired with أهلا in the classic welcome أهلا وسهلا! ('may you find family and smooth ground — welcome!').

examples.trans: Welcome! Please come into the courtyard.
A hundred welcomes to you all!

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علب.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a brimmed sun hat, straw hat, or cap.

examples.text: البس قبعة قش لما تمشي بالشمس.
examples.trans: Wear a straw hat when you walk in the sun.
Her floral hat is hanging on the door.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقلق, بيقلق).

examples.text: لا تقلقي يا مدام، هلا بنشوف البطاقة.
examples.trans: Do not worry, ma'am, we will check the tag right now.
We worried a little when the bus ran late.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكتب, بيكتب).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Form III defective verb used in Jordanian Arabic for meeting someone at a station or finding something.

examples.text: ننزل عالمحطة نلاقي طارق قبل الضهر.
examples.trans: Let's go down to the station to meet Tariq before noon.

examples.text: ما لاقيت القلم الأزرق على المكتب.
examples.trans: I didn't find the blue pen on the desk.

meanings.note: Means 'still' in affirmative sentences (لسا سليم 'still intact') and 'not yet' alone or with negation (لسا؟ 'not yet?').

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Literally 'play', and idiomatically ما حدا بيلعب معها / معي ('nobody messes with her / me').

examples.trans: We played ball in the courtyard.
Don't play this game with me.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative from مباشر ('direct'): immediately or without detours.

examples.text: من المحطة رح نروح مباشرة عالبيت.
examples.trans: From the station we will go straight home.
Write the note right after the lesson.

meanings.note: Form II active participle from بكر ('early morning'), used in formal/semi-formal phrases like الموعد المبكر ('the early appointment').

examples.text: القطار المبكر بيوصل الساعة سبعة الصبح.
examples.trans: The early train arrives at seven in the morning.

examples.text: هاد الصباح المبكر أهدى وقت بالشوارع.
examples.trans: This early morning is the quietest time on the streets.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مشاكل.

examples.trans: There is no problem at all with your booking.
Every problem has a simple solution.

مصفوف.gloss: lined up; parked neatly; arranged in rows

meanings.en: lined up; parked neatly; arranged in rows
meanings.note: Form I passive participle from صفّ ('to line up/park'): used for parked vehicles or pastries arranged in rows.

examples.trans: The buses are parked neatly in rows in front of the station.
The chairs are lined up in the garden for the guests.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from طبع ('to print'): used for printed timetables, tickets, and books.

examples.trans: The printed timetables are posted on the wall.

examples.text: جبنا نسخ مطبوعة من النوتات للفرقة.
examples.trans: We brought printed copies of the sheet music for the band.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Masculine noun with broken plural مقاطع, used for a musical passage, verse, or text excerpt.

examples.text: خلينا نعيد المقطع الوسطاني من الأغنية.
examples.trans: Let's repeat the middle section of the song.
This is the nicest passage in the whole story.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from قلّم ('to stripe/trim'): describes striped cloth, bags, or notebooks.

examples.text: شنطة القماش المقلمة كانت على الكرسي.
examples.trans: The striped canvas bag was on the chair.
He wore a blue shirt striped with white.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكالمات.

examples.trans: An important phone call came in on the landline.
She finished the call in two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from كرّم ('to honour'): used for distinguished guests.

examples.trans: The guest of honour arrived early for the reception.
We welcomed the honoured teachers in the hall.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نجوم.

examples.trans: The sky is clear and full of stars tonight.
The guesthouse service deserves five stars!

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
